The map \(T_\alpha\to V\) has closed image: its graph is closed since \(V/S\) is separated, and projection from the product with the proper \(S\)-scheme \(T_\alpha\) is proper. Its image is still quasi-finite over \(S\). A finite union of these closed images contains \(E_r(K)\), is proper with finite fibres over \(S\), and is finite by AU.6/AW.

Shrink \(S\) once more so that \(Rr_*K\) has locally constant cohomology, using Proposition 3.2 and the finite cohomological bound. BZ.2 again gives
\[
 r(E_r(K))=E_{\mathrm{id}_S}(Rr_*K)=\varnothing.
\tag{CA.7}
\]
Thus \(E_r(K)=\varnothing\). This proves the induction, with universal acyclicity throughout, rather than only for the original fibres.

In particular, for \(S=\operatorname{Spec}k\) the dense open is all of \(S\). Every finite-type \(V/k\) is universally locally acyclic relative to every bounded constructible \(K\). After change of base this gives
\[
 V\times Y\longrightarrow Y
 \quad\text{universally locally acyclic relative to }\operatorname{pr}_V^*K.
\tag{CA.8}
\]
The proper constructibility input to (CA.7) is the curve-and-proper-support proof of Proposition 3.2; it does not use the generic-local-acyclicity statement being proved here.

### CA.4. The cone from incidence controls transverse tests

Let \(X\) be smooth and \(C\subset T^*X\) closed and conical, containing the zero section. A map \(h:U\to X\) of smooth schemes is \(C\)-transverse when \(\ker(dh)\) meets \(C\times_XU\) only in zero. In that case the image
\(h^\circ C=dh(C\times_XU)\) is closed and conical. To prove closedness, work on an affine chart and write the map as a map of nonnegatively graded algebras. Modulo the positive-degree ideal of the target algebra, its source algebra has only the zero vertex set-theoretically. Its positive-degree generators are therefore nilpotent modulo that ideal, so the quotient is finite over degree zero. Lift finitely many homogeneous generators of this quotient. Induction on degree shows that their lifts generate the source as a module over the target. The restricted map of cones is finite and its image is closed.

A map \(f:U\to Y\) is \(h^\circ C\)-transverse when \((df)^{-1}(h^\circ C)\) contains no nonzero covector of \(Y\). Since \(h^\circ C\) contains zero, this condition makes \(df\) injective; the coordinate Jacobian criterion AE.1 makes \(f\) smooth. Both transversality conditions are open: the bad locus is the proper image of the projectivization of the corresponding closed cone of kernel vectors. We say that \(K\) is micro-supported on \(C\) if every such transverse pair \((h,f)\) has \(f\) locally acyclic relative to \(h^*K\). The proof below gives universal local acyclicity for its pairs.

Put \(P=\mathbf P^n\), \(G=\mathcal RF\), and let \(E=E_p(p^{\vee *}G)\subset Q\), as in BZ.5. Let \(C_F\) be its cone, with the zero section adjoined. We prove that \(F\) is micro-supported on \(C_F\).

For a transverse pair \(P\xleftarrow{h}U\xrightarrow{f}Y\), form \(Q_U=U\times_PQ\), with \(p_U:Q_U\to U\) and \(p^\vee_U:Q_U\to P^\vee\). Proper base change gives
\[
 h^*(\mathcal R^\vee G)
 =Rp_{U,*}p_U^{\vee *}G[n-1].
\tag{CA.9}
\]
We show that \(fp_U\) is universally locally acyclic relative to \(p_U^{\vee *}G\).

Away from \(E_U=U\times_PE\), the map \(p_U\) is universally locally acyclic for that complex by the definition of \(E\) and base change. The map \(f\) is smooth, so CA.2 proves the desired assertion there. At \((u,H)\in E_U\), the map
\[
 (p^\vee_U,fp_U):Q_U\longrightarrow P^\vee\times Y
\tag{CA.10}
\]
is smooth. Here is the differential check. Let \(x=h(u)\), \(y=f(u)\), and let \(\lambda\subset T_x^*P\) be the conormal line of \(H\). The cotangent space of \(Q\) is the pushout of \(T_x^*P\) and \(T_H^*P^\vee\) over their common conormal line. This follows by differentiating the single incidence equation \(\langle x,H\rangle=0\); the two derivatives are nonzero and give that common line. Since \(p\) is smooth, base change to \(U\) identifies the cotangent space of \(Q_U\) with the pushout of \(T_u^*U\) and \(T_H^*P^\vee\) along \(\lambda\). Thus injectivity of the cotangent map in (CA.10) is exactly injectivity of
\[
 \lambda\oplus T_y^*Y\longrightarrow T_u^*U,
 \qquad(\xi,\eta)\longmapsto dh(\xi)+df(\eta).
\tag{CA.11}
\]
The first transversality condition says \(dh\) is nonzero on \(\lambda\). The second says its image cannot meet \(df(T_y^*Y)\) nontrivially, and that \(df\) is injective. These are exactly the needed assertions. The Jacobian criterion makes (CA.10) smooth near \(E_U\).

The product projection \(P^\vee\times Y\to Y\), with the complex pulled back from \(G\), is universally locally acyclic by (CA.8). Smooth change of source in CA.2 applies to (CA.10). This proves the desired assertion near \(E_U\), and hence everywhere on \(Q_U\). Proper transport BZ.2 and (CA.9) imply universal local acyclicity of \(f\) relative to \(h^*\mathcal R^\vee G\).

In the inversion triangle (BZ.13), the other term \(L_F\) has locally constant cohomology. Its inverse image under \(h\) is locally constant; smoothness of \(f\) gives universal local acyclicity for that term by AT. The defect-cone triangle now gives the assertion for \(h^*F(-(n-1))\), and therefore for \(h^*F\). We have proved
\[
 F\text{ is micro-supported on }C_F,\qquad
 \dim C_F\le n.
\tag{CA.12}
\]
Extension by zero to projective space and restriction prove the same existence and dimension bound for every bounded constructible complex on \(\mathbf A^n\).

Two consequences follow directly from the definition. If \(h\) is \(C\)-transverse and \(K\) is micro-supported on \(C\), then \(h^*K\) is micro-supported on \(h^\circ C\). Indeed a transverse test after \(h\) composes to a transverse test before \(h\): if the composite differential kills a covector of \(C\), transversality for the second map first forces its image to be zero, and transversality for \(h\) then forces the covector to be zero. The condition on the test function is preserved by the same image calculation. Also microsupport conditions are closed under triangles, finite sums, direct summands and invertible locally constant twists, since each corresponding defect cone has those properties.

### CA.5. The Cartier comparison from a locally acyclic parameter

Let \(f:X\to\mathbf A^1\) be smooth, \(i:D=f^{-1}(0)\to X\), and \(j:X\setminus D\to X\). If \(f\) is locally acyclic relative to \(K\), then the canonical map
\[
 K\otimes Rj_*\kappa\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K
\tag{CA.13}
\]
is an isomorphism. We prove it on geometric stalks; outside \(D\) it is the identity.

At \(x\in D\), replace the base by its strict henselian trait at \(0\), with generic point \(\eta\) and geometric generic point \(\bar\eta\). Let \(I\) be its absolute Galois group. The stalk of the right side of (CA.13) is
\[
 R\Gamma(X_{(x)}\times\eta,K)
 \simeq R\Gamma\!\left(I,
       R\Gamma(X_{(x)}\times\bar\eta,K)\right).
\tag{CA.14}
\]
The last comparison is ordinary Galois descent. One can construct it by the Čech resolutions of finite Galois extensions of \(\eta\). Their geometric nerves are finite sets with the same insertion contraction as CA.1. Taking the filtered system of finite extensions gives continuous group cochains. The totalization computes the displayed derived invariants; for bounded-below coefficients every total degree has the usual finite range of nonnegative Čech degrees. AS continuity identifies the geometric-fibre limit in this construction.

Local acyclicity gives the \(I\)-equivariant isomorphism
\[
 K_x\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X_{(x)}\times\bar\eta,K).
\tag{CA.15}
\]
The action on \(K_x\) is trivial: its evaluation map comes from sections on \(X_{(x)}\), on which \(I\) acts trivially. Smooth local acyclicity gives the same assertion for the constant coefficient \(\kappa\). A bounded finite-dimensional complex commutes with the group-cochain construction under tensor product. This is checked first for one finite-dimensional vector space, a finite direct sum of copies of \(\kappa\), and then by the finitely many truncation triangles of \(K_x\). Equations (CA.14)–(CA.15) therefore identify the stalk of (CA.13) with the isomorphism
\[
 K_x\otimes R\Gamma(I,\kappa)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(I,K_x).
\tag{CA.16}
\]
The maps are the actual cup/evaluation maps of the Čech resolutions. No claim about the dimension of inertia cohomology or a trivialization of \(K\) on the whole strict localization is needed.

Take the fibres of (CA.13) and of the identity map \(K\to K\), using the open–closed localization triangles. Closed projection and the exact closed-support equivalence give
\[
 i^*K\otimes i^!\kappa\xrightarrow{\sim}i^!K.
\tag{CA.17}
\]
This is the usual coefficient map for exceptional inverse image: transpose the closed counit and compare the two localization triangles to identify it. BJ.6's smooth-pair orientation gives \(i^!\kappa=\kappa_D(-1)[-2]\). Thus (CA.17) is the canonical comparison with that twist and shift.

### CA.6. Noncharacteristic exceptional inverse image

Suppose \(X,W\) are smooth separated finite-type \(k\)-schemes, \(K\) is micro-supported on a cone \(C\) containing zero, and \(h:W\to X\) is \(C\)-transverse. Then
\[
 h^*K\otimes h^!\kappa\xrightarrow{\sim}h^!K.
\tag{CA.18}
\]
For \(\dim W=m\) and \(\dim X=n\), the orientation is \(h^!\kappa=\kappa_W(m-n)[2(m-n)]\).

First let \(h\) be a closed immersion of codimension \(c\). Near a chosen point of \(W\), choose functions \(f_1,\ldots,f_c\) cutting it out whose differentials extend to a basis of the cotangent space of \(X\). Such functions are obtained by lifting a basis of its conormal space; smoothness of \(W\) and the coordinate Jacobian criterion give a smooth map to \(\mathbf A^c\) with this zero fibre after shrinking. Every intermediate zero locus is smooth.

Transversality says that the span of \(df_1,\ldots,df_c\) meets \(C\) only in zero along \(W\). In particular the first parameter \(f_1\) is \(C\)-transverse there; openness lets us shrink so that it is transverse near the chosen point. Microsupport makes \(f_1\) locally acyclic relative to \(K\), and CA.5 proves the first Cartier comparison. After restriction to \(f_1=0\), CA.4 gives microsupport on the image cone. The remaining differential span still meets that image only in zero: lifting an intersection would put a covector of \(C\) in the original span. Repeat for \(f_2,\ldots,f_c\). The resulting composite is (CA.18). Compatibility follows by transposing the successive counits; their composite is the counit for the composed closed immersion. BJ.6 supplies the product orientation \((-c)[-2c]\).

For general \(h\), factor it as its closed graph \(W\to W\times X\), followed by the smooth projection to \(X\). The pullback of \(C\) under that projection is transverse to the graph exactly when \(h\) is \(C\)-transverse: a covector in the graph's conormal annihilates its tangent precisely when \(dh\) kills the corresponding covector of \(X\). Smooth pullback gives microsupport for the pulled-back complex by CA.4. The closed-graph case and the smooth exceptional orientation of BJ/BV prove (CA.18), with shift \(2(m-n)\) and twist \(m-n\). The coefficient comparisons compose because their adjoint counits compose; this identifies the resulting map with the canonical one for \(h\).

Thus the cone bound in BZ is a microsupport bound with the canonical exceptional comparison for transverse fibres. Appendix CB applies these results to a quadratic coordinate change at infinity, including characteristic two and finite-field choices.

For local acyclicity and transversality, see [Illusie's appendix to Deligne's *Théorèmes de finitude*, §§1.1 and 2.2–2.7, in the author-hosted SGA \(4\frac12\)](https://publications.ias.edu/node/378), [Beilinson, version 7, §§1.2–1.3 and 3.3–3.5](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.06768v7), and [Saito, version 4, §7.4](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.03018v4). CA.5 gives the needed exceptional comparison directly through the trait and its canonical evaluation map; it does not assume a characteristic-cycle pullback formula.

## Appendix CB. A quadratic projection with constant boundary comparison

We prove (BY.26) over the finite or algebraically closed ground fields of BY–CA. Put \(m=n+1\geq2\), write
\(T=\mathbf A^n\times\mathbf A^1\), and let
\[
 j:T\longrightarrow\overline T=\mathbf A^n\times\mathbf P^1,
 \qquad D=\overline T\setminus T.
\tag{CB.1}
\]
For a bounded constructible \(\kappa\)-complex \(K\), choose a proper closed \(Y\subset T\) outside which its cohomology is locally constant. Such a set exists by the finite constructible partitions of those finitely many cohomology sheaves. We will find an automorphism \(g\) for which \(g^{-1}Y\) is finite over \(\mathbf A^n\) and
\[
 i_b^*Rj_*g^*K\longrightarrow
 Rj_{b,*}i_{b,T}^*g^*K
\tag{CB.2}
\]
is an isomorphism for every geometric point \(b\) of the base. A finite extension of a finite ground field is allowed. Here \(i_b\) is the compactified fibre map and \(i_{b,T}\) its restriction to \(T\). The arrow is the base-change map obtained from the open adjunction unit.

### CB.1. Choosing a boundary point and a direction

Use coordinates \((x_1,\ldots,x_n,s)\) on \(T\), and embed it in \(\mathbf P^{n+1}\) by
\[
 j'(x,s)=(1:x_1:\cdots:x_n:s).
\]
Write \(\overline Y\) for the projective closure of \(Y\). On the chart \(y_1\ne0\) consider the smooth affine space \(W\), with coordinates \((z,u_2,\ldots,u_n,v)\), and the finite map
\[
 \sigma:W\longrightarrow\{y_1\ne0\},\qquad
 (z,u_2,\ldots,u_n,v)\longmapsto
 (z^2:1:u_2:\cdots:u_n:v).
\tag{CB.3}
\]
The divisor \(D'=\{z=0\}\) maps isomorphically to this chart of the hyperplane at infinity. Let
\(H=\mathbb D_TK\). On the smooth open \(T\setminus Y\), this is the locally constant dual complex with twist \(m\) and shift \(2m\), by BJ and BV. In particular its cohomology is locally constant there.

Apply CA.4 to the bounded constructible complex
\[
 L=\sigma^*j'_!H
\]
on \(W\). We obtain a closed conical microsupport \(C\subset T^*W\), containing zero, of dimension at most \(n+1\). There is a dense open \(Q\subset D'\) such that every geometric fibre \(C_q\) has dimension at most one. Here is an algebraic proof of this uniform bound.

Write \(D'=\operatorname{Spec}A\), where \(A\) is a polynomial ring in \(n\) variables over \(k\), and put \(F=\operatorname{Frac}A\). The closed subset \(C|_{D'}\) is affine and has finitely many irreducible components. Remove the closures of the images of the components which do not dominate \(D'\). For a remaining reduced component \(Z=\operatorname{Spec}B\), dominance makes \(A\to B\) injective. The transcendence-degree calculation in M.1 gives
\[
 r=\operatorname{trdeg}_{F}\operatorname{Frac}B
   =\dim Z-n\leq1.
\]
Apply the monic-elimination argument of K.1 over the field \(F\). It gives algebraically independent \(t_1,\ldots,t_r\in B\otimes_A F\) such that \(B\otimes_A F\) is finite over \(F[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\). That argument uses only polynomial relations and division by a nonzero field element, so it applies in every characteristic.

Choose finitely many \(A\)-algebra generators \(b_1,\ldots,b_s\) of \(B\). Each \(t_i\) belongs to \(B_f\) after inverting one nonzero \(f\in A\). Enlarge \(f\) by the finitely many denominators in the coefficients of monic equations for the \(b_j\) over \(F[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\). Their equations then have coefficients in \(A_f[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\). The inclusion of this polynomial algebra into \(B_f\) is injective, since the \(t_i\) are independent over \(F\). The bounded powers of the \(b_j\) in their monic equations generate \(B_f\) as a module over it, by K.1. Thus
\[
 A_f[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\longrightarrow B_f
 \quad\text{is finite.}
\]
After tensoring with any geometric residue field \(\Omega\) at a point of \(\operatorname{Spec}A_f\), the resulting algebra is finite over \(\Omega[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\). For each prime of this fibre algebra, its domain quotient is integral over a quotient of the polynomial algebra. The fraction-field extension is algebraic, so its transcendence degree is at most \(r\), again by K.1. Consequently every irreducible component of that geometric fibre has dimension at most \(r\leq1\); an empty fibre contributes nothing. Taking the product of the finitely many choices of \(f\), and the preceding open complement of the nondominating images, gives the required dense open \(Q\). No flatness, equidimensionality or minimality of the microsupport is needed.

Shrink \(Q\) to avoid \(\sigma^{-1}\overline Y\). This still leaves a dense open. A component of \(\overline Y\) is the closure of a component meeting \(T\), so it cannot be the hyperplane at infinity. Its intersection with that hyperplane has smaller dimension, by the dimension calculation in M.1/Y. Thus \(\overline Y\) does not contain the whole chart \(D'\).

A closed conical subset of a vector space of dimension at most one is zero together with finitely many lines, after algebraic closure. To see this, projectivize its nonzero part; the projectivization is zero-dimensional and of finite type, hence is a finite set. Its inverse image is precisely those lines. Consequently, over each \(q\in Q\), there is a nonempty open set of tangent vectors of the form
\[
 (1,w)\in k\oplus k^n,\qquad w\ne0,
\tag{CB.4}
\]
which are not annihilated by any nonzero covector in \(C_q\). Each of the finitely many lines excludes a proper affine hyperplane in \(w\)-space: a nonzero functional \(\alpha\,dz+\beta\,du\) cannot vanish identically on all \((1,w)\). The condition on \((q,w)\) is open, because its failure is the image of a closed incidence subset of the projective cone \(\mathbf P(C|_Q)\). Projection is proper.

The linear transformations of \(T\) fixing \(x_1\) include
\[
 a(x_1,y)=(x_1,Ay+b x_1),
 \qquad y=(x_2,\ldots,x_n,s),\quad A\in\mathrm{GL}_n.
\tag{CB.5}
\]
Their lifts to \(W\) are \(\widetilde a(z,u)=(z,Au+b)\), and
\(\sigma\widetilde a=a\sigma\). Starting at the origin of \(D'\) with tangent vector
\(\tau=(1,0,\ldots,0,1)\), these lifts reach every pair in (CB.4): choose \(b=q\) and an invertible \(A\) carrying the last basis vector to \(w\). Such an \(A\) exists by extending each nonzero vector to a basis. We can therefore choose \(a\) so that
\[
 a(c)\notin\overline Y,\qquad
 C^a_0\cap\tau^\perp=\{0\},
 \quad c=(0:1:0:\cdots:0),\quad
 C^a=\widetilde a^\circ C.
\tag{CB.6}
\]
The complex \(\sigma^*j'_!a^*H=\widetilde a^*L\) is micro-supported on \(C^a\), by CA.4.

Over an infinite ground field the required open in the affine parameters of (CB.5), with \(\det A\ne0\), has a rational point: a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on every point of affine space over an infinite field. The latter assertion follows by induction on the number of variables and the one-variable root bound. Over a finite field the same argument works after a finite extension whose cardinality is greater than the degrees of a nonzero polynomial defining a principal open inside the required open. Inductively choose each coordinate outside its finite forbidden root set. Thus all the coordinate choices occur over one finite extension, not over an unspecified infinite algebraic extension.

### CB.2. The quadratic map and finite bad locus

Set
\[
 h(x_1,\ldots,x_n,s)=(x_1+s^2,x_2,\ldots,x_n,s),
 \qquad g=ah.
\tag{CB.7}
\]
The inverse of \(h\) subtracts \(s^2\), so this is an automorphism in every characteristic. It extends to
\[
 \overline h:\overline T\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{n+1},
 \qquad
 (x,(s:t))\longmapsto
 (t^2:t^2x_1+s^2:t^2x_2:\cdots:t^2x_n:st).
\tag{CB.8}
\]
These coordinates have no common zero: \(t\ne0\) makes the first nonzero, while \(t=0\) makes the second nonzero. The whole \(D\) goes to \(c\).

By (CB.6), the closed subset
\(\overline h^{-1}a^{-1}\overline Y\) misses \(D\) and equals \(g^{-1}Y\) on \(T\). It is proper over \(\mathbf A^n\). Its geometric fibres are proper closed subsets of \(\mathbf P^1\) missing infinity, hence are finite. Properness and AU.6/AW make
\[
 g^{-1}Y\longrightarrow\mathbf A^n
\tag{CB.9}
\]
finite. This proves finiteness scheme-theoretically after giving the closed subset its reduced structure; no assumption that its projection is flat is used.

### CB.3. Boundary transversality when \(2\) is invertible

Near \(D\), write the projective coordinate as \((1:t)\). Adjoin a variable \(v\) with
\[
 v^2=1+t^2x_1,\qquad v=1\text{ along }D.
\]
Restrict to \(v\ne0\) and \(v+1\ne0\). This is an étale neighbourhood \(e:V\to\overline T\), since \(2v\) is invertible, and its inverse image of \(D\) is exactly the selected copy \(v=1\). There is a lift of \(\overline h e\) through \(\sigma\):
\[
 \kappa:V\longrightarrow W,\qquad
 (x,t,v)\longmapsto
 \left(t/v,\ t^2x_2/v^2,\ldots,t^2x_n/v^2,\ t/v^2\right).
\tag{CB.10}
\]
Substitution in (CB.3) verifies this equality of morphisms. Along the selected copy of \(D\), the equation for \(v\) gives \(dv=0\). Hence \(\kappa(D)=0\), all tangent vectors to \(D\) map to zero, and
\[
 d\kappa(\partial_t)=\tau.
\tag{CB.11}
\]
By (CB.6), \(\kappa\) is \(C^a\)-transverse along \(D\), and therefore on an open neighbourhood of it by CA.4. Open-extension base change identifies
\[
 \kappa^*\sigma^*j'_!a^*H=e^*j_!g^*H.
\tag{CB.12}
\]
Indeed both sides are the indicated pullback on \(t\ne0\) and have zero geometric stalks on \(t=0\); the open-extension adjunction gives the canonical identification.

CA.4 now gives microsupport on \(\kappa^\circ C^a\). At any point of \(D\), (CB.11) puts this cone inside the line generated by \(dt\), together with zero. The conormal space of a fibre of \(V\to\mathbf A^n\) is spanned by \(dx_1,\ldots,dx_n\), and meets that line only in zero. Thus the fibre immersion is transverse at the boundary. CA.6 applies there. This only requires containment in the conormal line; no equality of singular supports or characteristic-cycle pullback theorem is being assumed.

### CB.4. Characteristic two and purely inseparable base change

In characteristic two an equation \(v^2=1+t^2x_1\) would not define an étale neighbourhood. Instead let \(q:\mathbf A^n\to\mathbf A^n\) square \(x_1\) and leave the other coordinates fixed, and let \(\overline q=q\times\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf P^1}\). These maps are finite universal homeomorphisms: on affine charts, and after any base change, their algebra has the form \(A[z]/(z^2-a)\), finite free with basis \(1,z\). Over an algebraically closed geometric field the polynomial is \((z-\sqrt a)^2\), so every geometric fibre is nonempty with one point. This proves surjectivity and universal injectivity as well as integrality. The composite \(\overline h\,\overline q\), on \(1+t x_1\ne0\), lifts through \(\sigma\) by
\[
 \chi(x,t)=
 \left(
 \frac{t}{1+t x_1},
 \frac{t^2x_2}{1+t^2x_1^2},\ldots,
 \frac{t^2x_n}{1+t^2x_1^2},
 \frac{t}{1+t^2x_1^2}
 \right).
\tag{CB.13}
\]
The equality \((1+t x_1)^2=1+t^2x_1^2\) proves the lift. Direct differentiation at \(t=0\) gives \(\chi(D)=0\), zero differential on \(TD\), and \(d\chi(\partial_t)=\tau\). Consequently (CB.6), CA.4 and CA.6 give the same transverse fibre comparison for
\[
 \chi^*\sigma^*j'_!a^*H
   =\overline q^*j_!g^*H
\tag{CB.14}
\]
near \(D\).

We will descend the desired ordinary base-change statement through \(\overline q\). The arbitrary-base equivalence (BE.7a), proved in BE.4, applies to \(\overline q\), its open restriction and each of their base changes. Their inverse-image functors are exact equivalences, with exact direct-image inverses. For a cartesian open-immersion square this proves the actual comparison
\[
 \overline q^*Rj_*M
   \xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_*q_T^*M.
\tag{CB.15}
\]
For example, apply the conservative exact inverse \(\overline q_*\); composition of direct images identifies the result with \(Rj_*M\), and the adjunction units identify the resulting arrow with the identity. This also proves compatibility with restriction to any geometric fibre. Furthermore proper duality and \(q_T^!=q_T^*\), the two adjoints to the exact equivalence \(q_{T,*}\), give
\(\mathbb D(q_T^*M)=q_T^*\mathbb D M\). Thus (CB.14) is precisely the dual coefficient complex required for (CB.2) after the base change \(q\). A cone vanishing after \(\overline q^*\) vanishes before it. This proves descent without asserting that singular support itself is unchanged by a radicial morphism.

### CB.5. Duality identifies the actual fibre-comparison map

Let \(b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\mathbf A^n_k\) be the selected geometric point. We may replace \(\Omega\) by its algebraic closure \(L\): the extension is purely inseparable, so BE.4 identifies the fibre topoi and the actual open direct-image comparison. The point then has an \(L\)-rational lift to \(\mathbf A^n_L\). To relate its comparison to (CB.2), note that the ground field \(k\) is perfect. Every finitely generated \(k\)-subalgebra of \(L\) is a domain and, by the separating-normalization argument in M.1, becomes smooth over \(k\) after inverting a nonzero element. That localization still embeds in \(L\). Two such smooth subalgebras are contained in a third by adjoining both finite lists of generators and localizing again. Their union is \(L\), so \(\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k\) is an affine inverse limit of smooth morphisms. Let \(p:\overline T_L\to\overline T\) and \(p_T:T_L\to T\) be the projections. AS.7, applied to the qcqs open immersion \(j\), gives the canonical isomorphism \(p^*Rj_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{L,*}p_T^*E\) for every bounded constructible coefficient complex \(E\) used here. Composition compatibility of that comparison identifies (CB.2) at \(b\), after the preceding conservative field extension, with the comparison at its rational lift. Thus it suffices to prove the latter for each selected geometric point.

The same extension preserves the dual coefficient complex. For a constructible \(\kappa\)-sheaf \(F\) on \(T\), use the resolution in M.5 by finite sums of \(u_!\kappa\), with \(u\) affine étale of finite presentation. For a bounded-below \(\kappa\)-complex \(B\), formula (M.9) computes each term of internal derived Hom as \(Ru_*u^*B\). AS.7 identifies its pullback with \(Ru_{L,*}u_L^*p_T^*B\), by the canonical comparison. If \(B\) starts in degree \(c\), the resolution spectral sequence has indices \(r\geq0\), \(s\geq c\), so only finitely many terms occur in each total degree. Exact pullback and these termwise comparisons therefore give \(p_T^*R\mathcal Hom(F,B)\simeq R\mathcal Hom(p_T^*F,p_T^*B)\). Finite cohomology triangles give the same statement for bounded constructible \(F\). These are the evaluation comparisons of M.5: the termwise maps are adjunction mates and commute with the resolution differential. Both \(T/k\) and \(T_L/L\) are smooth of dimension \(n+1\), so BJ identifies their structural dualizing complexes with \(\kappa(n+1)[2n+2]\), compatibly with extension of the field. Taking this complex for \(B\) proves \(p_T^*\mathbb D_kF\simeq\mathbb D_Lp_T^*F\), preserving evaluation. Exact base change for open extension by zero consequently identifies the pullback of \(j_!\mathbb D_kF\) with \(j_{L,!}\mathbb D_Lp_T^*F\).

The cone used above remains a microsupport after that extension. Here is why this holds for our particular cone. In CA.4 it is constructed by extension to projective space, the Radon transform and the closed universal non-acyclicity locus \(E\). Open extension and the proper Radon transform commute with extension of fields. Outside the pullback of \(E\), universal local acyclicity still holds by its definition. Thus the newly constructed defect locus, and then its cone, are contained in the pulled-back old ones. CA.4 applied over the algebraically closed extension proves microsupport on the smaller cone, hence also on the larger one. This argument applies to an algebraic closure of the residue field of any base point, including a nonclosed one. It does not replace that point by a closed point of the original base.

Write \(M=g^*K\), or \(q_T^*g^*K\) in CB.4. On the open complement of the corresponding finite bad locus in \(\overline T\), the restriction of \(M\) to \(T\) is locally constant. Near the boundary, CB.3 or CB.4 makes the compactified fibre immersion \(i_b\) transverse to a microsupport of \(j_!\mathbb D M\). Its codimension is \(n\). CA.6 and BJ's orientation give the canonical identifications
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 i_b^!j_!\mathbb D M
 &\simeq i_b^*j_!\mathbb D M(-n)[-2n]\\
 &\simeq j_{b,!}\bigl(i_{b,T}^*\mathbb D M(-n)[-2n]\bigr)\\
 &\simeq j_{b,!}\mathbb D_b(i_{b,T}^*M).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{CB.16}
\]
The last equality uses local constancy on this punctured neighbourhood and the smooth orientations: the ambient dimension is \(n+1\) and the fibre dimension is one. Both duals include their actual twists and shifts. It is not an assertion that this equality holds through the arbitrary singularities on \(Y\).

Dualizing (CB.16), using biduality and the open and closed exchange maps in BJ/BV, gives
\[
 i_b^*Rj_*M\simeq Rj_{b,*}i_{b,T}^*M
\tag{CB.17}
\]
near the boundary. This is the map in (CB.2), not merely an isomorphism between its source and target. To check the map, transpose the coefficient comparison in the first line of (CB.16); CA.6 identifies it by the closed counit. The second line is the open-extension pullback comparison, and its adjoint is the open unit. Their pasted adjoint is therefore the restriction of \(M\to Rj_*M\), which defines (CB.2). This is also the unit/counit description of the dual exchange maps used here.

On \(T\), (CB.2) is the identity and requires no transversality assumption, including at \(Y\). In odd characteristic the boundary check descends from the étale neighbourhood \(V\), since quasi-isomorphisms are detected on geometric stalks. In characteristic two it descends by (CB.15). This proves (CB.2) everywhere, for every geometric base point.

Finally enlarge the finite closed bad locus by the section \(s=0\). Its projection is now finite and surjective, and the locally constant complement has only become smaller. The comparison (CB.2) concerns \(K\) itself and is unchanged by this enlargement. Thus all parts of (BY.26) hold. The first-reduction, finite-extension descent and target-effacement arguments of BY.7 give the stated integral and rational realization in every dimension over the ground fields used there. This deduction retains the coefficient-comparison and recursive foundational hypotheses of those arguments; it does not assert the unrelated nearby-cycle or weight theorems.

The free primary comparison is [Barrett, *The derived category of the abelian category of constructible sheaves*, version 1, Theorem 2.1 and Lemma 3.1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.10859v1). The argument above only uses the microsupport bound and the canonical comparison proved in CA. Characteristic two is handled by descending (CB.2) through the base universal homeomorphism, with the maps explicitly identified in (CB.13)–(CB.15).

- [Stacks, profinite groups and cohomology] The Stacks Project, [Section 59.57](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A2H) and [Section 9.22](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BMI). Free comparisons for continuous group cohomology and infinite Galois theory. Appendix AA gives the continuous-cochain, finite Sylow and restriction calculations used in R.3–R.4.
- [Stacks, field sites and divisors] The Stacks Project, [Tag 02GL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02GL), [Tag 03QR](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03QR) and [Section 59.68](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RH). Free comparisons for étale field objects, their Galois sets and the divisor sequence. Appendix AB supplies the local algebra, finite-cover descent, slice calculation and uniformizer lifts used in R.3–R.5.
- [Stacks, images and open maps] The Stacks Project, [Tag 054K](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/054K), [Tag 01UA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01UA) and [Tag 00HR](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00HR). Free comparisons for constructible images, flat openness and faithful flatness. Appendix AC proves the Noetherian image and prime-lifting statements and the finite-cover basis needed by Appendix S.
- [Stacks, Picard descent] The Stacks Project, [Tag 03P7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03P7), [Tag 03C4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03C4) and [Tag 023T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/023T). Free comparisons for the Picard identification and faithfully flat descent. Appendix AD gives the rank, effective-family, degree-one and rigidification arguments used here.
- [Stacks, Picard geometry prerequisites] The Stacks Project, [Tag 00TA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00TA) and [Tag 01W7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01W7). Free comparisons for smooth local coordinates and projective properness. Appendix AE proves the flatness, graded closed-image and geometric-integrality steps used in P and Q.
- [Stacks, curve constants] The Stacks Project, [Tag 01XL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XL) and [Tag 01XM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XM). Free comparisons for the affine-cover cohomology and base-change calculations. Appendix AF gives the finite-over-projective finiteness, localization and connected-fibre proofs used in O.4.
- [Stacks, normalization and normal curves] The Stacks Project, [Tag 032L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032L), [Tag 00PD](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00PD) and [Tag 00TV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00TV). Free comparisons for finite normalization, normal curve local rings and the separable-residue smoothness criterion. Appendix AG connects the trace and local algebra calculations to the completion in O.1.
- [Stacks, finite diagrams and inseparable extension] The Stacks Project, [Tag 01Z6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01Z6), [Tag 01ZO](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZO) and [Tag 0BRA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BRA). Free comparisons for eventual affineness, eventual finiteness and purely inseparable change of the underlying space. Appendix AH proves the boundary and localization assertions and connects the finite diagram to the programme limit proofs.
- [Stacks, constructible compactness] The Stacks Project, [Tag 0901](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0901). Free comparison for compactness of the constructible topology. AI.3 uses the affine ultrafilter proof in the earlier constructible-sheaf lesson and gives its exact role in obtaining a single refinement for a finite family of sheaf maps.
- [Stacks, ramification] The Stacks Project, [Galois extensions and ramification, Section 15.114](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09E3), and [profinite inertia, Tag 0BUA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BUA). Free comparisons for finite and profinite inertia. AJ.1–AJ.3 prove the needed strict smooth-curve case from the trace bound, a uniformizer filtration, prime-to-characteristic root extensions and explicit continuous cohomology.
- [Stacks, cohomological limits] The Stacks Project, [continuity, Tag 09YQ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09YQ), [filtered coefficients, Tag 03Q5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03Q5), and [limits of bases, Tag 03Q6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03Q6). Freely accessible comparison statements and proofs. AK.1–AK.3 give the finite-object, finite-cover and hypercover-cochain descent proof needed for the Noetherian models used here.
- [Stacks, finite and smooth comparison] The Stacks Project, [finite direct images, Tag 03QN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03QN), [smooth base change, Tag 0EYQ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYQ), [generic-cover extension, Tag 0EYJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYJ), and [smooth connected-fibre neighbourhoods, Tag 0EY4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EY4). Free comparison proofs. AL.1–AL.4 give the finite-algebra, curve-invariance and étale-limit arguments used here; AR.1–AR.5 prove the generic-cover extension required by AL.5, and AS.1–AS.7 give the positive-degree cohomological induction over a fixed field with the exact finite-model and two-induction arguments.
- [Stacks, components along a section] The Stacks Project, [base change of the distinguished component, Tag 055M](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/055M), [generic component spreading, Tag 055N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/055N), [the open neighbourhood criterion, Tag 055Q](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/055Q), and [geometric connectedness near a generic fibre, Tag 055G](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/055G). Free geometric comparisons for AM.1–AM.4.
- [Stacks, points and slices] The Stacks Project, [separable closed points, Tag 056U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/056U), [étale slices, Tag 057G](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/057G), and [discrete valuation specializations, Tag 054F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/054F). Free comparison proofs for the point and specialization constructions in AM.4–AM.6.
- [Stacks, formal section comparisons] The Stacks Project, [completion along a smooth section, Tag 05D5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05D5), [punctured power-series full faithfulness, Tag 0EY9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EY9), [bundle comparison from functions, Tag 0EKP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EKP), and [restriction of finite étale covers, Tag 0EL8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EL8). Free comparison proofs for AN.2–AN.6.
- [Stacks, algebra extension and relative purity] The Stacks Project, [finite extension across depth-two complements, Tag 0EY6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EY6), [reflexive extension, Tag 0EBJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EBJ), [power-series purity, Tag 0EYA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYA), and [purity in smooth families, Tag 0EYB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYB). Free statements for the coherent-extension and relative-purity problems treated in AO.1–AO.6. The kernel and regular-pair proofs there apply to arbitrary Noetherian bases; the integral-scheme reflexive-hull argument is not needed.
- [Stacks, finite algebra tests] The Stacks Project, [the trace criterion for finite étale algebras, Tag 0BJF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BJF), and [the flat local fibre criterion, Tag 00U6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00U6). Free comparison statements for AO.3; the local-equation and trace arguments are given there.
- [Stacks, flat change of base] The Stacks Project, [flat base change, Tag 02KH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02KH), and [finite free realization of a residue extension, Tag 07NE](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NE). The degree-zero equalizer argument is AO.2; the local monic-tower construction is AO.5.
- [Stacks, regular local purity] The Stacks Project, [regular local purity, Tag 0BMA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BMA), [lifting purity, Tag 0BLS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BLS), and [the depth-three case, Tag 0BLM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BLM). AP.1–AP.5 give the regular-local proof using the coherent extension kernel, completion and a finite residue-field splitting extension.
- [Stacks, DVR degrees and roots] The Stacks Project, [the degree formula, Tag 09E8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09E8), [Galois transitivity, Tag 09EA](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09EA), [common ramification indices, Tag 09EB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09EB), [root extensions, Tag 09EV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09EV), and [Abhyankar’s lemma, Tag 0BRM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BRM). AP.6–AP.7 prove the degree and root-base-change statements needed for the Galois situation here.
- [Stacks, remaining divisor extension] The Stacks Project, [extension over a regular boundary, Tag 0H2W](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H2W), [the divisor case, Tag 0EYE](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYE), [tame local structure, Tag 0EYG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYG), [the normalization model, Tag 0EYH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYH), and [the transverse section test, Tag 0EYI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYI). AQ.1–AQ.2 prove the regular-boundary extension and AQ.4–AQ.5 give a graded descent proof of the DVR-family case. The broader tame local model is not required by that descent proof.
- [Stacks, gluing near a point] The Stacks Project, [gluing in a closed fibre, Tag 0BQ5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BQ5), and [spreading the finite étale property, Tag 0EY3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EY3). AQ.1 gives the finite multiplication-table and denominator-clearing proof used to add the codimension-one points; AR.2 proves the base-local gluing with its finite-chart hypotheses.
- [Stacks, actions and finite covers] The Stacks Project, [equivariant sheaves and gradings, Tag 03LE](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03LE), and [finite étale morphisms, Tag 0BL6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BL6). AQ.3 proves the fibrewise identity test, and AQ.4 writes the coefficient calculation for the action of the roots-of-unity group over a ring.
- [Stacks, extension over a normal base] The Stacks Project, [generic Galois cover extension, Tag 0EYJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYJ). AR.1–AR.5 give the splitting, base-local gluing and completed-section argument, and explicitly remove the temporary quasi-compactness restriction on the smooth family.
- [Stacks, smooth comparison induction] The Stacks Project, [smooth base change, Tag 0EYQ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYQ), Lemma 59.89.1, the first proof of Theorem 59.89.2, and Lemma 59.89.3. Freely accessible comparison arguments; Appendix AS proves pointed finite-group effacement, finite replacement of the vanishing problem, the two cohomological inductions and bounded-below comparison over a fixed field, with field-based normalization and explicit continuity arguments.
- [Stacks, strict-local acyclicity] The Stacks Project, [local acyclicity, Tag 0GJM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GJM), Definition 59.93.1, Proposition 59.93.2 and Lemma 59.93.3. Freely accessible comparison statements and proofs. Appendix AT supplies strict-local stalk and base-change identifications, arbitrary allowed constant groups, bounded-below locally constant cohomology, and the selected-neighbourhood colimit used in the affine-line argument.
- [Stacks, proper coherent geometry] The Stacks Project, [Chow modification, Tag 0200](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0200), [proper coherent images, Tag 02O3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02O3), [formal functions, Tag 02O7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02O7), and [Noetherian Stein factorization, Tag 03H0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03H0). Freely accessible statements and proofs. AU.1–AU.6 give the projective-coordinate, support-induction, completion and connectedness arguments, followed by the proper finite-fibre consequence.
- [Stacks, approximation and connectedness] The Stacks Project, [absolute approximation, Tag 07RN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07RN), [general Chow modification, Tag 0202](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0202), [fibre idempotents, Tag 0G7X](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G7X), and [general Stein factorization, Tag 03H2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03H2). Freely accessible proofs. AV.1–AV.6 give the finite-data deductions, nonaffine ambient construction, projective coordinates, proper thickenings and connectedness argument.
- [Stacks, quasi-finite factorization] The Stacks Project, [Tag 03GD](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03GD), [Tag 03GE](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03GE), [Tag 00UH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00UH), [Tag 00UI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00UI), [Tag 00UJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00UJ), [Tag 02LN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02LN), [Tag 03GW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03GW), [Tag 05K0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05K0). Freely accessible proofs. AW.1–AW.6 prove the integral-closure comparison, finite-piece construction, nonaffine finite factorization and finite refinement of étale coverings, using the specified earlier programme algebra and limit proofs.
- [Stacks, henselian sections] The Stacks Project, [Tag 09XI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09XI), [Tag 09Z8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z8), [Tag 09ZG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZG), [Tag 095S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095S). Freely accessible comparison proofs for henselian pairs and degree-zero proper restriction. AX.1–AX.7 give the ring, spectral-space, finite-map and sheaf arguments at the stated arbitrary-base scope.
- [Stacks, proper sections] The Stacks Project, [Tag 03N0](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03N0), [Tag 09XM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09XM), [Tag 09XN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09XN), [Tag 0A3H](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A3H), [Tag 00I7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I7), [Tag 0A3I](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A3I), [Tag 03Q9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03Q9), [Tag 095S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095S). Freely accessible comparison statements. AY.1–AY.6 prove descent of opens and sheaf sections, geometric field invariance, section continuity and the canonical proper degree-zero base-change formula.
- [Stacks, constructible embeddings] The Stacks Project, [Tag 03RY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RY), [Tag 09Z5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z5), [Tag 09Z4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z4), [Tag 09YU](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09YU). Freely accessible comparison statements. AZ.1–AZ.6 prove finite presentations, compactness, affine-limit descent, the normal-generic section calculation and finite-direct-image embeddings of constructible coefficients.
- [Stacks, finite effacement] The Stacks Project, [Tag 04D1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04D1), [Tag 0EZN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZN), [Tag 03Q6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03Q6), [Tag 03AJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03AJ). Freely accessible comparison statements. BA.1–BA.7 prove affine étale lifting, closed-subscheme constant-coefficient vanishing, arbitrary-base higher continuity and finite-cover and torsion-sheaf effacement.
- [Stacks, henselian cohomology] The Stacks Project, [Tag 0EM7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EM7), [Tag 09Z8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z8), [Tag 0A51](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A51). Freely accessible comparison statements. BB.1–BB.4 prove the henselian-neighbourhood construction, affine torsion comparison, module-injective acyclicity and the affine-covering bound; BB.5 identifies the proper torsor-lifting input proved in BD.6.
- [Stacks, proper cover algebraization] The Stacks Project, [Tag 0885](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0885), [Tag 088C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088C), [Tag 0BQC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BQC). Freely accessible comparison statements. BC.1–BC.6 prove coherent algebraization and finite-cover and torsor lifting over complete Noetherian pairs, and the complete-local projective-line comparison. BD.3–BD.6 supply pointed approximation and extend the finite-cover and projective-line results to arbitrary henselian local bases.
- [Stacks, finite cover descent and pointed approximation] The Stacks Project, [Tag 01ZM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZM), [Tag 07QY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07QY). Freely accessible limit and approximation statements. BD.1–BD.2 prove finite-cover descent. BD.3–BD.6 use the earlier programme regular-completion and smooth-factorization proofs to establish pointed approximation, henselian proper finite-cover lifting and projective-line comparison.
- [Derived-complete inverse image, Tag 099K](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099K), and [constant Noetherian coefficients, Tag 099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N). Free comparisons for the completed adjunction and operation maps in BL; the explicit proofs are given there.
- [Proper–open exchange, Tag 0F7A](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F7A), and [derived lower shriek via compactifications, Tag 0F7H](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F7H). Free comparisons for the exchange, refinement, composition and base-change constructions used in BM; its completed coefficient and inverse-limit proofs are written there.
- [Uniform constructible coefficient bounds, Tag 09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2). Free comparison for BN.1; its Tor filtration and descent to the étale coefficient category are proved explicitly there.
- [Finite-coefficient local structure, Tag 09BI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BI), [stabilization, Tag 09C5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C5), and [adic local structure, Tag 09C6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C6). Free comparisons for BO; its finite Tor induction, compatible matrices, finite-image stabilization and internal-Hom lifting give the complete local-model proof at the stated coefficient scope.
- [Strict coefficient-system normalization, Tag 03UN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UN), and [finite-level kernels, Tag 03UP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UP). Free comparisons for BP; its common stratification, uniform torsion bound, quotient recovery and full degree-zero equivalence are proved there.
